column1: Our direct land use change (dLUC) methodology uses spatial data to identify tree cover loss and land use change (LUC) emissions due to deforestation on the location boundaries provided. This version of the GHG emissions analysis assumes that only one commodity is cultivated in each location provided; the accuracy of results will depend on how well the locations provided reflect crop areas. If more than one commodity is cultivated in any of your locations or if your locations contain non-crop areas (e.g. reserve areas), please follow the allocation guidelines provided in the GHG protocol's Land Sector and Removals' documentation to allocate appropriately. This analysis is unable to separate emissions from non-crop areas, it will estimate a production for the entire location provided. GFW Pro is not responsible for verifying supply chain traceability of locations. Methods for verifying traceability are provided in the GHG protocol Land Sector and Removals' documentation.

column5: Data layer being used to calculate the emissions factor. Land management unit (LMU)-level direct land use change (dLUC): Emissions due to land conversion during the assessment period occurring directly on areas owned or controlled by the company OR lands in LMUs where the reporting company sources from and has full traceability to (LSRS, 2025).

column2: Location level GHG emission factor related to crop commodity production.
column5: Tonnes of CO2 per tonne of commodity produced. The emission factor is calculated by dividing the discounted GHG emissions by the production of the crop in the location. Production is calculated by multiplying the crop yield by the polygon area. For any uploaded locations that don't include a user-specified yield value, the analysis will use a default yield based on the list's specified commodity. Default yield is calculated using the Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM) pixel-level yield values, and take into account crop intensity (crop rotation). The analysis uses a weighted average of the per-pixel yield value, weighted over the harvested area. These values are aggregated at the location level, which ensures a more representative yield value for the location.
